teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: friend, neighbour, classmate, colleague, boss, partner, know, meet, work, study, university, building

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
friend, neighbour, classmate, colleague, boss, partner, know, meet, work, study, university, building
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How do you know each other? (asking origin of relationship)
• We work together (stating shared activity)
• He is my neighbour from next door (describing acquaintance)
• We met at university (explaining background)

teacherNotes.title: Phonetic Focus
teacherNotes.content: Pronunciation of /g/ and /k/ sounds in 'colleague', 'classmate'. Neutral stress in 'neighbour'.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus:
Pronunciation of /g/ and /k/ sounds in 'colleague', 'classmate'. Neutral stress in 'neighbour'.

teacherNotes.title: Grammar Function
teacherNotes.content: Present Simple of verbs 'know', 'meet' + Prepositions of origin and context (at work, from university)

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Present Simple of verbs 'know', 'meet' + Prepositions of origin and context (at work, from university)
Controlled Practice:
You study together in the same university class. Who is he?
Reading Script & Dialogue:

A: Who is Alex?
B: He is my colleague at work. We work in the same office.
A: How long do you know him?
B: We know each other for two years.
Listen to conversations about neighbours and classmates, noting how the speakers met.
